name: Content

hero.title: A typo in your frontmatter fails the build. Not your readers.
hero.lede: Write docs and blogs in Markdown or MDX. Zero compiles every page to real Pyreon components at build time, checks each frontmatter block against your schema, and writes the search index, sitemap, RSS feed and llms.txt for you.

facts.value: .md and .mdx compiled to Pyreon JSX<small>Real elements at build time, not an HTML string.</small>
any Standard Schema validator<small>Zod, Valibot, ArkType or `@pyreon/validate`. The package ships none.</small>
the pyreon.dev docs and blog<small>200+ Markdown pages, 59 of them with live examples.</small>

why.title: A content site that checks itself.

items.title: Frontmatter that cannot lie
items.text: Give a collection a schema. Drop the `title` from a post and the build stops with `src/content/blog/hello.md: frontmatter does not match collection "blog" schema`, followed by the field and the reason. Your types come from the same schema.

items.title: Live examples are real files
items.text: `<Example file="./examples/counter" />` mounts a real `.tsx` file inline, so it is type-checked, linted and refactored with the rest of your code. Give two examples the same `share` key and they share one signal: click in one, the other updates.

items.title: Search with no service
items.text: The build writes a search index per collection, and `<Search>` opens it with Cmd+K and loads it lazily. No crawler, no API key, and it works in `vite dev` too.

items.title: Merge today, publish on Monday
items.text: Name a date field with `publishDate` and a post dated in the future stays out of lists, search and feeds until that day; add `unpublished: 'omit'` and it is not even bundled. pyreon.dev/blog schedules its posts this way.

difference.title: Delete the content loader you wrote by hand.

demo.spec: Same behaviour as the reference, with the real error text. When `title` or `description` is missing, the output panel shows: `[@pyreon/zero-content] src/content/docs/install.md: frontmatter does not match collection "docs" schema (N issues):` followed by one line per missing field, `  - title: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` (Zod 4 wording), then `build failed`. Use `@pyreon/zero-content` built-ins where they render in the browser (`Callout` for the tip).

features.title: Everything a docs site or blog needs, built in.

items.name: Markdown and MDX to Pyreon JSX
items.text: at build time, so the compiler and tree-shaking work on your prose (Shiki code blocks are the one HTML island)

items.name: Typed collections
items.text: `getCollection`, `getEntry` and `getEntries`, typed from your schema through a generated `.pyreon/content-types.d.ts`

items.name: Components without imports
items.text: drop a PascalCase `.tsx` into `src/mdx/` and use it in any page by name; an unknown name fails the build with a did-you-mean

items.name: Live `<Example>` blocks
items.text: real `.tsx` files mounted inline, with `share` keys for state that spans two examples

items.name: Directives
items.text: `:::tip`, `:::warning`, `:::note`, `:::danger`, `:::info`, `:::code-group`, `:::math`, `:::mermaid`, `:::details`, and a warning when you type `:::warn`

items.name: Shiki code blocks
items.text: light and dark themes baked into one render, filename labels, line numbers, `{2-3}` highlights and a copy button

items.name: Docs components
items.text: Tabs, PropTable, APICard, CompatMatrix, PackageBadge, Details, Mermaid, Math, Sidebar, Toc, Breadcrumbs and PrevNext

items.name: Search
items.text: a Cmd+K `<Search>` (or `useSearch` for your own UI) over a per-collection index written at build

items.name: Sitemap, RSS and llms.txt
items.text: from one `seo` option; the RSS feed can carry full articles for dev.to imports

items.name: Drafts and scheduled entries
items.text: `publishDate` plus `unpublished: 'omit'` keep future posts out of the bundle; `PYREON_CONTENT_NOW` builds the site as it will look on a later date

api.title: One config, a few queries, a box of components.

limits.title: Made for Zero
limits.text: Pages render through Zero's file router and render modes. You write the route (one `defineContentRoute` call, plus `getStaticPaths` and the collections import for static builds); the package has no standalone mode.

limits.title: Bring your own validator
limits.text: Nothing is re-exported: import `z` from Zod, or use Valibot, ArkType or `@pyreon/validate`. Any Standard Schema library works without an adapter.

limits.title: Pick the right draft mode
limits.text: By default an unpublished entry is left out of lists, search and feeds but still bundled, for preview on SSR sites. On a static site set `unpublished: 'omit'` (shipping in the next release) so a draft's text never reaches a public chunk.

limits.title: Scheduled means next build
limits.text: Scheduling lands in the next release. A static site decides what is published when it builds, so a post dated Monday appears with the first deploy on or after Monday. pyreon.dev runs a daily deploy for that reason.

recipes.title: A blog that publishes on schedule
recipes.text: Date a post in the future, merge it now. Production builds leave it out of the bundle, the RSS feed, the sitemap and search until its day, and the feed carries whole articles for readers and dev.to imports.

recipes.title: Two live examples, one shared signal
recipes.text: Each example is an ordinary component file. Give both the same `share` key and the button in one drives the readout in the other, inline in the page.

faq.q: Is the Markdown turned into an HTML string?
faq.a: No. Every Markdown node becomes a JSX element at build time, so your prose goes through the same compiler as your components. Shiki-highlighted code is the one exception: it arrives as pre-coloured HTML.
Any Standard Schema library: Zod, Valibot, ArkType, typia or `@pyreon/validate`. The package calls the standard `validate` method and ships no validator of its own.

`getCollection` skips `draft: true` entries in production. In the next release the search index, sitemap, RSS and llms.txt leave them out too, and with `unpublished: 'omit'` the draft is not bundled at all, which is what a static site wants.

faq.q: Does search need a server or a third-party service?
faq.a: No. The build writes JSON index files into your build output and the browser fetches them the first time search opens. In dev a middleware builds the same index on demand.

faq.q: Can I use it without Zero?
faq.a: No. The integration with Zero (its file router, render modes and image handling) is the point of the package. The SEO generators are the exception: `generateSitemap`, `generateRssFeed` and `generateLlmsTxt` are plain functions you can call from any script.

faq.q: Will my AI assistant see my content?
faq.a: Yes, through `@pyreon/mcp`: `get_content_collection` lists your collections and `get_content_entry` returns one entry's frontmatter and heading outline.
